topic: Transferring unused credits between spouses (line 32600, Schedule 2): a spouse can claim the unused part of the partner's current-year tuition (max $5,000 minus what the student needs to bring their own tax to zero), age, pension and disability amounts; carried-forward tuition cannot be transferred

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Sam, student in 2025, $8,000 of current-year tuition, net income $12,000 (below the 2025 basic personal amount of $16,129 → federal tax $0 before tuition, so Sam needs $0 of the tuition credit). Alex (spouse) claims $5,000 transferred on line 32600 → $5,000 × 14.5% = $725 less federal tax. The remaining $3,000 is carried forward by Sam only. Provincial amounts not included.

spoken_manual.bpa: 'under the basic personal amount' = $16,129 shown on screen

sources.spouse: canada.ca CRA line 32600 'Amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner': unused age amount, Canada caregiver amount for infirm children under 18, pension income amount, disability amount for self, tuition amounts; only if the partner did not need them to bring their federal tax to zero; carried-forward tuition cannot be transferred; Schedule 2
sources.cap: canada.ca CRA line 32400 (tax year 2025) and 'Transferring and carrying forward amounts': maximum transfer $5,000 minus the amount the student needs to reduce their own tax payable; only current-year amounts
sources.rate: 2025 lowest federal rate 14.5%; 2025 basic personal amount $16,129 (CRA What's new for 2025, cited in m30/data.json)
